newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING-AUSTRALIAN JOCKEYS FINED FOR STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-AUSTRALIAN JOCKEYS FINED FOR STRIKE.

text.p: The Australian Jockey Club stewards fined three Sydney riders on Monday for a weekend strike which left apprentices grabbing glory on the nation's race courses.

The AJC, which runs the sport in New South Wales state, fined jockeys John Marshall, Aaron Kennedy and Craig Carmody A$500 ($395) for each ride missed at a Sydney racecourse on Saturday under a rule that jockeys can be penalised for not fulfilling commitments without just cause.
Marshall was penalised a total of A$2,500 and Kennedy and Carmody were fined A$1,000 each. Nine other Sydney jockeys were also called before the stewards and were expected to be fined.
Australia's top jockeys called a snap one-day strike on Saturday in pursuit of a pay claim although most scheduled race meetings went ahead with apprentice riders in the saddle.
The jockeys are seeking an increase in the fee paid to them for riding a losing horse to a uniform A$130 per race, about double what jockeys are now paid.

Monday's fines were fixed after the AJC rejected an appeal by Sydney-based jockeys to adjourn the hearing. The appeal was presented to the stewards by Darren Beadman, winner on November's Melbourne Cup on Saintly.
The jockeys are still considering further strikes.
The New South Wales Totalisator Agency Board estimated on Monday that the strike had cost it A$3.6 million in lost betting turnover throughout the country.
